expect.arrive: Downtown Salt Lake City is flat and walkable; Temple Square and the Capitol both have their own free lots, Ensign Peak's trailhead lot is a small gravel pull-in in a residential street.
expect.parking: Temple Square and Capitol lots are large and rarely full midday; Ensign Peak's lot holds maybe 15 cars and street parking fills on weekends.

paths.do: Walk the plaza, Assembly Hall exterior, and grounds.
Temple Square, then drive up to the Capitol steps and rotunda.
Capitol, Temple Square, plus the short climb up Ensign Peak for the skyline view.

alt: Ensign Peak Salt Lake City overlook
Salt Lake Temple Square Assembly Hall
Salt Lake City skyline from Capitol Hill

trail.from: Ensign Peak Nature Park trailhead, 1002 N Ensign Vista Dr

expect.arrive: Both food stops are quick roadside/downtown stops; Logan Canyon is a two-lane mountain highway with occasional pull-outs, driven at dusk on this itinerary.

paths.do: In-N-Out only, eat in the car on the way north.
In-N-Out snack, then a proper dinner at Osteria Amore before the drive.

alt: Downtown Salt Lake City restaurant row evening

expect.arrive: A 5am start on US-89 through farm country, then Bear Lake's turquoise water comes into view at Garden City; Montpelier is a small Idaho town, Jackson is a proper mountain town with metered downtown parking.

paths.do: Photo stops at overlooks only, no museum or beach time.
Pull off at Bear Lake State Park for 20-30 minutes on the sand.
Bear Lake beach, Butch Cassidy Museum in Montpelier, and a proper coffee/bakery stop in Jackson.

alt: Garden City Utah Bear Lake shoreline
Jackson Wyoming Town Square antler arch

expect.arrive: Teton Park Road turnouts are all direct pull-offs, most with room for 5-15 cars; the Teton Range comes into full view starting at Windy Point and stays in frame the rest of the drive.
expect.parking: Small paved turnouts at each named stop; none have ever been reported full, they're too brief a stop for that.

paths.opt: Drive it, stop for photos only
paths.do: Pull into 3-4 of the best turnouts (Windy Point, Mount Moran, Jackson Point) without getting out for long.
Same turnouts plus 30-40 minutes inside Craig Thomas Discovery and Visitor Center.
All eight turnouts and the homestead, a few minutes at each.

alt: Teton Range from Teton Park Road
Grand Teton Climbers Ranch historic cabins
Craig Thomas Discovery and Visitor Center

expect.arrive: Jackson Lake turnouts line the shoreline; Signal Mountain Summit Overlook is a few minutes' detour up a paved side road, the rest are direct roadside pull-offs.

paths.do: Skip the Signal Mountain side road, stop at the lakeside overlooks and the dam.
Detour up Signal Mountain Summit Road for the highest view on the drive.

expect.arrive: This is the golden-hour run down the valley; Snake River Overlook and Schwabacher Landing are both short walks from small gravel lots that get busy right at sunset, Mormon Row's barns are visible from the parking areas.
expect.parking: Snake River Overlook has about 16 spaces, Schwabacher Landing about 20 — both fill in the last hour before sunset in good weather.

paths.do: Snake River Overlook and the Moulton Barn at Mormon Row only.
Same two plus the short walk in to Schwabacher Landing's beaver ponds.
All named stops including Teton Point, Glacier View, and Blacktail Ponds.

alt: Mormon Row T.A. Moulton Barn sunset

expect.arrive: Teton Village is a small alpine-style base area with cafes right off the parking; Death Canyon Trailhead is a dirt/gravel lot at the end of a bumpy unpaved road past the Rockefeller Preserve.
expect.parking: Death Canyon Trailhead lot is small (room for roughly 20-25 cars) and can fill by mid-morning on weekends in good weather; the Preserve Center has a larger paved lot a short drive before it.

paths.do: Persephone Westbank and a walk around Teton Village, skip the hike.
Village, then drive to the Preserve Center and walk a few minutes onto the trail without going to the full overlook.
Village, then the out-and-back to Phelps Lake Overlook from Death Canyon Trailhead.

alt: Teton Village Jackson Hole base area
d03s1.seasonal: The Jackson Hole Aerial Tram at Teton Village runs through October 4, 2026, so it is still operating on this date if they want a ride up the mountain instead of the hike.

expect.arrive: Jenny Lake Visitor Center sits above a large paved lot that fills by mid-morning in September; the shuttle boat leaves from a dock a short walk below the visitor center and runs continuously, no reservation.
expect.parking: Jenny Lake's main lot is one of the busiest in the park; if it is full there is overflow parking a short walk further from the dock.

paths.opt: Boat there and back, no hike
paths.do: Round-trip boat ride across and back without leaving the west dock.
One-way or round-trip boat, then the climb to Inspiration Point and back to the dock.

paths.opt: Skip the boat, walk the shoreline
paths.do: Hike the South Jenny Lake Trail around to Inspiration Point and back without the boat.

d03s2.seasonal: The Jenny Lake shuttle boat's 2026 season ends September 30 and narrows to 9am-5pm from September 8 onward, so it is running but on shortened hours on this date (jennylakeboating.com).

trail.from: Jenny Lake Visitor Center, hiking the shoreline without the boat
Jenny Lake Boat Dock, west shore

expect.arrive: Jenny Lake Road is a one-way scenic loop with pull-outs; String Lake Picnic Area has a gravel/paved lot right at the shallow, warm south end of the lake, popular with families.
expect.parking: String Lake's lot is moderate-sized and fills on warm weekend afternoons; arriving mid-afternoon on a Sunday should be fine.

paths.do: String Lake Picnic Area, Cathedral Group Turnout, and the roadside overlooks, no lake walk.
Walk part of the String Lake shoreline out and back instead of the full loop.
The complete flat loop trail around the lake.

expect.arrive: Jackson Town Square is compact and entirely on foot, with the four antler arches at the corners; the wildlife art museum is a short drive north of downtown.
expect.parking: Downtown Jackson has metered street parking plus a few public lots; it's tightest right around dinner time.

paths.do: Walk the square, dinner nearby.
Square, dinner, then a drink at the Million Dollar Cowboy Bar.
Squeeze in the wildlife art museum before it closes, then dinner and the square.

alt: Jackson Wyoming Town Square antler arches
National Museum of Wildlife Art Jackson
